title: Air Pollution and Air Quality

cards.h: Winter smog is a yearly headline
cards.b:
Every winter Delhi and the Indo-Gangetic Plain choke on smog. UPSC asks about the Air Act, AQI, NCAP, BS-VI, stubble burning and health. Mains wants causes, policy and a way forward.

The numbers below matter in Prelims. The causes and policy gaps matter in Mains.

Primary pollutants are released directly: SO2, NOx, CO, particles. Secondary pollutants form in the air: ground-level ozone and PAN.

PM2.5 and PM10 are particles under 2.5 and 10 micrometres. PM2.5 enters the lungs and blood and causes the most harm. Other pollutants: lead, ammonia, benzene, benzo(a)pyrene, arsenic, nickel.

Photochemical smog (Los Angeles type) needs sunlight, NOx and volatile organic compounds. It makes ozone and peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN).

Classical or sulphurous smog (London 1952) comes from coal smoke and SO2 in cold, humid air. The Great Smog of 1952 led to the UK Clean Air Act 1956. Delhi’s winter smog combines both with temperature inversion.

India’s National Ambient Air Quality Standards (2009) cover 12 pollutants. The annual limit for PM2.5 is 40 µg/m3 and the 24-hour limit is 60. For PM10 they are 60 and 100.

The National Air Quality Index was launched in 2014 with six bands: Good, Satisfactory, Moderate, Poor, Very Poor and Severe. The WHO guideline (2021) is much tighter: 5 µg/m3 annual for PM2.5.

The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1981 follows the Stockholm conference. It set up the CPCB and State Boards and allowed air pollution control areas. The Environment Protection Act 1986 provides the umbrella rules.

For Delhi NCR, the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) was set up in 2020 and given statutory form in 2021. The Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) imposes steps as AQI worsens.

The National Clean Air Programme (January 2019) targets about 130 non-attainment cities. It began with a 20 to 30 percent cut in PM goal by 2024 against 2017, later revised to 40 percent by 2025–26. Money flows through the PRANA portal and the 15th Finance Commission’s performance grants.

Bharat Stage VI fuel and engine norms started in April 2020, skipping BS-V. Other steps: Ujjwala LPG, power plant FGD rules, EV push (PM E-DRIVE), and subsidies for crop residue machines.

Main sources are vehicles, road dust, construction, coal power plants, industry, biomass cooking and crop-residue burning in Punjab and Haryana in October-November.

Studies differ on shares because meteorology varies. Transport and dust dominate in Delhi on most days; stubble contributes a large spike in some weeks. Indoor air from solid-fuel cooking remains a major rural killer.

Odd-even schemes, smog towers and cloud seeding trials give visible action but little evidence of big impact. Critics say the airshed approach across states is the real need, with enforcement on industry, transport and power.

Another debate: tighten standards to WHO levels or make them achievable first? A third: is air quality a health emergency or a development trade-off?

Many studies rank cities in the Indo-Gangetic Plain and parts of the North-East among the most polluted in the world. The health burden includes asthma, COPD and early deaths.

The Sustainable Development Goals and the Right to Life (Article 21) frame clean air as a right. Courts have repeatedly directed Delhi on vehicles, fuel and construction dust (M.C. Mehta cases).

Mains-style: “Why does northern India suffer from severe air pollution every winter? Suggest measures.” Structure: causes (inversion, stubble, vehicles, dust); health and economic cost; current measures (NCAP, GRAP, CAQM, BS-VI); gaps; airshed approach, crop diversification, public transport.

Prelims tip: Learn six AQI bands, the NAAQS year (2009), NCAP (2019) and BS-VI (2020). Air Act is 1981; Water Act is 1974.

quiz.q: The National Clean Air Programme was launched in:

quiz.w: Ozone forms by chemical reactions in the air.

quiz.q: The Air Act in India was passed in:
NAAQS in India were notified in:
Which Bharat Stage came into force in April 2020?

quiz.w: It was set up for the National Capital Region and adjoining areas.
It led to the UK Clean Air Act 1956.

quiz.q: The AQI in India was launched in:
Which pollutant is the most harmful to lungs and blood?
quiz.w: PM2.5 is fine enough to reach the bloodstream.
India’s standard is 40 µg/m3 annually, so the WHO value is far stricter.
